{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The agreement is unusually strong for us on the substantive risk allocation: indemnification (§ 20), IP and Customer Data ownership (§ 14), licence scope (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9.4 / § 29.4), renewal economics (§ 8), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), warranties (§ 19), audit rights (§ 22), insurance (§ 18) and governing law/venue (§ 28) all meet our preferred positions. There is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN or minimum-volume obligation binding us, and § 7.6 gives us a Vendor-side MFN in our favour.

Two issues require redlines, and both sit in walk-away territory notwithstanding their low playbook severity rating:

1. **§ 7.7 liquidated damages payable by Customer** — 15% of annual Fees per week, triggered by a ten-day payment delay. On the verified analysis this would exceed remaining contract value in roughly seven weeks.
2. **§ 21.1 liability cap basis** — because "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as only the Implementation Fee, fixed by § 1.6 at a one-time USD 12,000 in the first Order Form, the mutual cap is effectively USD 12,000, below our six-month floor. The same narrow definition hollows out the § 21.3 statement that Customer's payment obligation is not damages.

One process point: the § 21 finding did not clear automated verification (see § 4). We should confirm the § 1.5 / § 1.6 / § 21.1 cross-references against the execution copy before the redline goes out.

---

## 2. Findings table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification | Preferred position in full; indemnities are Excluded Claims under § 21.3. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables | Customer owns data and Deliverables; § 15.1 bars model training and cross-customer use. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control | § 24.4 bars Vendor repricing/termination on our change of control. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities | § 12.3 affirmatively confirms no exclusivity; § 12.4 restrains Vendor, in our favour. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence | Affiliates and contractors covered; perpetual paid-up licence in § 13.2. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities | No field-of-use or competitive restraint on Customer. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination | § 9.4 plus 30 days' notice under § 29.4; no Vendor convenience exit. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights | Annual, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, no system access. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution | New York law, New York County courts; no arbitration provision. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes | § 7.6 MFN runs in our favour; not redlined. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope | § 2.1 confirms no minimum or purchase commitment. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities | None present; § 12.3 expressly preserves our hiring freedom. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return | Six months' assistance at expiring Order Form rates; no withholding for fee disputes. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties | Tiered remedy with termination and refund; disclaimer does not swallow express warranties. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance | Limits match our model, term plus one year. |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) | 15% of annual Fees per week on a 10-day payment delay; no fallback available. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Liability cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability | Cap basis limited to the § 1.5/§ 1.6 Implementation Fee (USD 12,000) in the first Order Form. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

Both open deviations are identified in the verified findings as walk-away territory. We should treat them as conditions of signature:

- **§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** Our playbook position is no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer; the fallback (an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees) is unavailable because this is a payment-delay charge, not a termination fee. **Proposed redline:** flip § 7.7 so that no liquidated damages or penalty is payable by Customer, leaving Vendor's other late-payment remedies and § 7.3 untouched.
- **§ 21.1 — illusory liability cap.** The mutual cap resolves to USD 12,000, below our six-month floor. **Proposed redline:** reset the § 21.1 cap basis to the greater of the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, and widen the § 21.3 payment carve-out to amounts due under this Agreement. Mutuality, the § 21.2 damages exclusion and every Excluded Claim stay as drafted.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Confirm the § 21 cross-references.** The LOL-CAP finding is marked verification "fail"; we should read § 1.5, § 1.6 and § 21.1 against the execution copy to confirm the cap base before issuing the redline.
2. **Re-check the § 7.7 language.** That finding is marked "repaired", so we should confirm the final redline text tracks the clause as drafted.
3. **Issue a two-issue markup only.** Send § 7.7 and § 21.1/21.3 as our sole substantive changes and note to Vendor that we are accepting §§ 8, 11, 13, 14, 18–20, 22, 24 and 28 as drafted, which should make the ask easy to close.
4. **Escalate if resisted.** If Vendor will not move on either item, bring it back to the deal team before signature; on the verified analysis neither risk is one we can price.
5. **No other action required.** All remaining rules are compliant, and Vendor-favourable-to-us terms (§ 7.6 MFN, § 12.4, § 24.4, SLA credits) are being left untouched by design."}
